subject: Datacore private fleet: throughput and network sizing review
messages:
From: Amelia Rhodes <amelia.rhodes@datacore.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: platform_ops@datacore.com
Date: 2026-10-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private fleet sizing + network review for DataCore

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at DataCore is excited to move forward with a VPC-based private deployment for our inference stack. Before procurement we need a technical sizing and network assessment that maps to our throughput targets so we can lock on the hardware and network egress expectations. High level: we need to support 1,500 concurrent requests for our recommendation endpoint (average request = 1,200 tokens, p50 latency target <140ms, p95 <350ms). Workload mix: 70% short (<=256 tokens), 30% long (~1200 tokens).

Questions we need clarified for purchasing:
- Recommended minimum GPU count and type for sustained 75% utilization with 25% headroom.
- Network egress sizing per rack/pod (we need to budget for VPC egress).
- Warmup / cache strategy so cold-starts don't blow our latency SLOs.
- Preferred scaling topology (horizontal pods vs larger single-GPU pool).

Can your team produce a concise sizing memo (numbers + assumptions) plus any network configuration notes we should give to our infra team? Two-week timeline preferred.

Attached: initial service-level targets we shared internally.

Best,
Amelia
Amelia Rhodes
Head of Platform, DataCore

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private fleet sizing + network review for DataCore

Amelia — thanks for the clear targets. Happy to drive the sizing memo and a short network note. Quick clarifying questions so our assumptions line up:

1) Model: are you planning to serve a single model variant (production decoder-only ~13B) or plan for fallback sharded / smaller-quantized replicas for peak hours?
2) SLA: is the p50/p95 latency requirement a hard SLA per request or a target for the recommendation route only?
3) Burst pattern: is peak traffic short-lived (minutes) or sustained (hours)?

Initial thinking (very rough): for the workload you described, we expect a single A100 80GB-equivalent can handle ~18 concurrent short requests (<=256 tokens) at p50 targets with batching tuned; for long requests (~1200 tokens) the concurrency per GPU drops to ~3–4 depending on quantization. To meet your steady 1,500 concurrent requests with the 70/30 mix at 75% utilization and 25% headroom, ballpark GPU count is in the 22–28 A100 80GB-class range. If you prefer denser/cheaper instances (A10G or 80GB H100), numbers shift — we should run a lightweight microbench to confirm.

Network: rough egress budget is ~6–9 Gbps per GPU pod under full long-request load (TCP + TLS overhead included). We'll include SR-IOV recommendations and a NAT/egress sizing note for the VPC.

I'll assemble a short memo and a sizing XLS. Grace and Dylan (cc'd) will add the detailed network egress math and deployment topology. Proposed deliverable: 3-page memo + sizing workbook by 2026-10-15. Does that timeline work?

Action: Can you share a sample 1-hour traffic trace (or RPS/CPU/memory per-minute) if available — that will let us refine data-plane headroom assumptions.

Cheers,
Rafael
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Amelia Rhodes <amelia.rhodes@datacore.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-10T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet sizing + network review for DataCore

Thanks — I ran a quick back-of-envelope using the assumptions Rafael listed and adding network serialization overhead. Below is the digestable math so procurement can see the line items.

Assumptions:
- Production model: decoder-only ~13B; quantized Q4_0 for most replicas, but we recommend a small pool of full-precision for high-quality responses.
- Avg token generation rate (per long req): 70 tokens/sec (CPU/GPU combined wall-clock during generation).
- Short requests avg 60 tokens generated; long requests average 1,000 generated tokens (situation dependent).
- Batch efficiency: typical effective batch size = 8 for short, 4 for long on NVIDIA A100 80GB with our runtime.

Sizing math (simplified):
- Effective concurrent capacity per A100-80 (mixed load): 20 short-equivalent concurrents (weighted).
- Weighted concurrency required: 0.7*1500 + 0.3*1500 = 1500 (split used internally for lat calc). For CPU-normalized GPU count we compute using tokens/sec:
  - Short load tokens/sec = 0.7*1500*60 = 63,000 tps
  - Long load tokens/sec = 0.3*1500*1000 = 450,000 tps
  - Total tokens/sec = 513,000 tps
  - If one A100-80 can sustain ~20k tps (mixed, with quantization and batching), GPUs required = ceil(513k / 20k) = 26 GPUs

Headroom & robustness: add 25% buffer => 33 GPUs. If you accept a fallback tier (smaller 6–8 GPU pool of low-latency quantized models), we can reduce primary pool to ~26 and use fallback to absorb spikes.

Network egress: per-token serialization (UTF-8 + JSON) and TLS means ~120 bytes per token on average outbound. At 513k tps => ~62 MB/s => ~496 Mbps. But that's for payload only. Including response framing, metadata, and concurrent connections overhead, plan ~1.0–1.5 Gbps per 10 GPUs under mixed load. For a 33 GPU cluster, plan ~4–6 Gbps egress sustained, and allow headroom for bursts to 10 Gbps.

Deployment topology recommendation:
- 3–4 pods across 2–3 physical racks; each pod contains 8–12 GPUs (depending on chassis).
- Service mesh for request routing at edge, L7 routing within VPC to select quantized vs full-precision replicas.
- Prefix/KV caching: enable prefix caching for 35% of traffic (saves ~18% tokens/sec based on our eval).
- Warm pools: maintain 2–3 hot replicas per pod for <50ms cold-starts; pre-warm queues during deployment windows.
- Autoscale policy: target 70% GPU utilization, scale up stepwise with a 90s cool-down. Use a burst class (5–10% of capacity) for transient surges with prioritized fallback to quantized models.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Rafael to finalize memo and sizing sheet.
2) DataCore to provide 1-hour trace or representative RPS histogram.
3) Laura to own procurement template & egress billing estimate.

Attachment: network_egress_budget.pdf (detailed egress calc).

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
SRE / Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

Subject: Datacore private fleet: throughput and network sizing review — memo and next steps

Amelia / DataCore team — attached is the 3-page memo and the finalized sizing workbook. Summary decisions from our internal review: 

- Baseline: 26 A100-80GB-class GPUs to meet steady-state mixed workload at 75% utilization.
- Recommended procurement: commit to 33 GPUs (25% buffer) or 26 GPUs + a 6–8 GPU fallback quantized pool.
- Network: sustained egress ~5 Gbps for the full cluster with burst headroom to 10 Gbps. Recommend provisioning with dedicated egress IPs and SR-IOV-enabled NICs; avoid NAT gateways that throttle small persistent TLS flows.
- Topology: 3 pods across 2 racks, each pod sized for 8–12 GPUs. Use prefix caching and a small hot replica per pod.

Action items:
- DataCore: share 1-hour traffic trace (if available) by 2026-10-15 to finalize the microbench.
- Procurement: sign the provisioning agreement (DocuSign link below) so we can reserve capacity with the cloud partner.
- Redwood: we will spin up a 48-hour stress microbench when we have the trace; expected delivery 2026-10-22.

DocuSign: https://docu.sign/example/Datacore-Provisioning-Agreement
